newsitem.title: USA: Gov. orders California to repay $1.36 bln to Calpers.
newsitem.headline: Gov. orders California to repay $1.36 bln to Calpers.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Tuesday ordered the state to immediately repay its largest pension fund $1.36 billion, money the state improperly used to balance its budgets in the early 1990s.

Wilson, a Republican, said that by repaying the California Public Employees' Retirement System (Calpers) the entire amount during the 1997-1998 fiscal year, California taxpayers would save at least $650 million in interest.

State lawmakers had hoped to pay the money back over several years. But Calpers was "unwilling to offer an affordable" repayment plan, forcing the state to pay the money back in a lump sum out of its 1997-1998 budget, Wilson said.

Calpers is the largest public pension system in the United States with more than $100 billion in assets. Calpers manages retirement and health plans serving more than 1 million workers, retirees and their families.

A state appeals court ruled in February that the governor and the legislature improperly withheld the money from Calpers in the early 1990s to balance state budgets during California's deepest economic downturn since the Depression. In May, the state Supreme Court refused to rehear the case.
Wilson said repaying Calpers $1.36 billion this year would require lawmakers to sharply curtail their spending plans.
Funding for Wilson's proposed business tax cut would be eliminated, and money for most other non-education programmes could also be threatened, Wilson said.
Wilson directed the state's controller to immediately cut the check to Calpers.
